q.t: What is the name of the girl who welcomes us to her home?
q.e: Bela lives with her brothers Banku and Bishu.

q.t: What game do Bela and her brothers play outside?
q.e: They hide and look for each other.

q.t: Who is Shiru?
q.e: Shiru barks, wags his tail and is a member of the family.

q.t: What does Bela call her grandmother?
q.e: Her father's mother is Dadiji.

q.t: What do Bela's mother and Dadiji make on rainy days?
q.e: The family eats them together in the garden shelter.

q.t: Mother's sister is called…
q.e: Bua is father's sister.

q.t: Families can be…
q.e: "Families are big, families are small."

q.t: Which game did Bela and friends play in the park?
q.e: A ball knocks down a pile of stones.

q.t: Should we hurt or tease animals?
o: No — we should be kind to them
q.e: Banku and Bela never hurt Shiru and share food with him.

q.t: What is Munni very good at making?
q.e: She uses colours from dried flowers.

q.t: Can animals like cows and dogs be part of a family?
q.e: Families love and care for animals too.

q.t: Who helps with the housework in Bela's home?
q.e: Cooking, cleaning and shopping are shared.

q.t: How does Bela help her Dadaji?
q.e: Banku helps clean and chop vegetables.

q.t: What does Dadiji do for Bela every morning?
o: Takes her to school by car
q.e: She hums a song while doing it.

q.t: Kusum Mausi is Bela's mother's…
o: Close friend who is like a sister
q.e: Friends can feel like family.

q.t: What can be used to make a rangoli?
q.e: Many materials work.

q.t: Relatives who don't live with us are related through our…
q.e: Through mother or father.

q.t: Who needs special care in a family?
o: Grandparents, small children, or someone sick
q.e: We help them.

q.t: What do families do together in the evening in Bela's home?
o: Sit, talk and laugh in the garden
q.e: Spending time together makes families happy.

q.t: Who taught Bela and Banku old games?
q.e: Games he played as a child.

q.t: Why do families share housework?
o: So no one person gets too tired, and work gets done
q.e: Helping each other makes life easier and happier.

q.t: Father's brother is called…
q.e: Mama is mother's brother.

q.t: Why should we share food with animals that come home?
o: Caring for them is kind — they depend on us
q.e: Families care for animals and plants too.

q.t: Bela's family is…
q.e: Parents, grandparents, three children and Shiru.

q.t: What do we learn from elders?
q.e: Bela learnt songs from Dadiji.

q.t: Peek-a-boo is played with…
q.e: Hiding and suddenly reappearing.

q.t: Why did Dadaji ask the children to rest at the park?
q.e: Resting helps the body recover.

q.t: Antakshari is a…
q.e: Snakes and ladders is the board game.

q.t: Which shows love and care in a family?
o: Helping, sharing and spending time together
q.e: Love shows in what we do for each other.

q.t: Mother's brother is called…
q.e: His wife is Mami.

q.t: Who do we care for who is NOT in our family?
q.e: Caring reaches beyond our home.

q.t: Bela's father's mother is Dadiji. Bela's mother's mother is…
q.e: Nani and Nana are mother's parents.

q.t: Why do Bela's parents relax in the garden in the evening?
o: They are tired after a hard day's work
q.e: Spending time outdoors together helps them rest.

q.t: Which list is all games?
q.e: The others are food, vehicles and relatives.

q.t: A friend's mother whom we call Mausi shows that…
o: People who care for us can be like family
q.e: Kusum Mausi joins every festival at Bela's home.

q.t: Who is usually the oldest person in a family?
q.e: Answers can vary — ask your family!

q.t: Why does Bela make rangoli with fallen flowers instead of plucking them?
q.e: Caring for plants.

q.t: What makes every family special?
o: Its people care about each other
q.e: "My family is special, and yours is too!"

q.t: Who might live far away but still be family?
o: Relatives like uncles, aunts and cousins
q.e: We meet them on visits and festivals.

q.t: Ice cream at the park was bought by…
q.e: After about 20 minutes of rest.
